title: Microsoft Purview: sensitivity label protection policies for Microsoft Fabric items
summary: Hold: the summary promises that everyone outside the allowed list is blocked, despite the documented label-issuer exception. The automatic-label creator exception also needs its native-Fabric-item qualification; the roadmap facts, licensing discussion and documented commands are supported.

claims.where: title; front matter: products; What's changing
claims.claim: The roadmap describes Microsoft Purview manual labeling of Fabric items with access protections based on administrator-set policies.
claims.quote: This new functionality will allow users to manually label Fabric items with their sensitivity level and then apply access control protections based upon the protection policies set by administrators.

claims.claim: The Purview path through Information Protection, Policies, Protection policies, new policy and Microsoft Fabric reaches Define access control settings.
claims.quote: On the Define access control settings page, specify which users and groups should retain their access to items labeled with the sensitivity label you selected in step 4.
claims.fix: Use 'Information Protection > Policies > Protection policies > + New protection policy > Choose the sensitivity label used to detect sensitive items > + Add sensitivity label > sensitivity label > Choose data sources to apply the policy > Microsoft Fabric > Define access control settings > Add users and groups'. The omitted label selection chooses the policy's target and the printed route stops on the correct control page. The opening navigation and '+ New protection policy' are also supported by the already-cited https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/data-gov-protection-policy; the automatic missing-word finding is not a contradiction.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; controls[0].governs
claims.claim: A label-associated protection policy lets specified users and groups retain existing item permissions rather than granting new permissions.
claims.quote: Each protection policy for Fabric is associated with a sensitivity label. The policy controls access to an item that has the associated label by allowing users and groups specified in the policy to retain permissions they have on the item

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Everyone not on the policy's allowed list is blocked from the labeled item.
claims.quote: A protection policy doesn't apply to a label issuer. That is, the user that last applied a label associated with a protection policy to an item won't be denied access to that item, even if they aren't specified in the policy.
claims.fix: Replace the summary's first sentence with 'Purview protection policies restrict access to labelled Fabric items using an allowed list, with exceptions for label issuers and, for automatically labelled native Fabric items with no issuer, item creators.' In What's changing, replace 'and everyone else is blocked' with 'and other users are blocked, subject to the label-issuer and native-item creator exceptions described below'. In Why it matters and the impact rationale, qualify users left off the list with 'unless a documented label-issuer or native-item creator exception applies'.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: The user who last applied the policy-associated label retains access even when not named in the policy.
claims.quote: the user that last applied a label associated with a protection policy to an item won't be denied access to that item, even if they aren't specified in the policy.

claims.claim: Whenever a label is applied automatically with no issuer, the item's creator is unrestricted, without an item-type qualification.
claims.quote: For native Fabric item types, if the label is applied automatically by the system—such as in the case of downstream inheritance—and there is no designated label issuer, the user who created the artifact will not be restricted by protection policies.
claims.fix: Replace the automatic-label clause with 'and for native Fabric item types, where a label is applied automatically (for example by downstream inheritance) with no label issuer, the item's creator is not restricted'. The cited documentation limits this exception to native Fabric item types; do not extend it to Power BI semantic models.
